text:
Alex: Heads up — pushed a prototype mock for a 'savings waterfall' per-model card. Trying to land rules for how cache savings get split across routing tiers (sticky vs probabilistic) and model variants. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/mock/savings-waterfall.png  

Maria: Nice! quick q — are we crediting savings per-invocation or amortizing per-session? per-invocation looks noisy for short chats.  

Sam: I prefer hybrid: immediate credit to the route that saw the cache hit, then amortize a small pct across hotpath routes over a window (e.g., 24h). prevents noise and still rewards requesters. 70/30 is a starting point. :thinking_face:  

Rafi: Also we need to treat quantized variants as a different baseline. If route A uses int8 model, lower token unit price should be reflected as a model_sku delta, not a "cache saving". Otherwise we double-count.  

Ciara: Agreed. proposal: 3 buckets in the UI — model-sku delta (explicit price difference), cache-hit credit, and prefetch/prefill credit. show an "uncertainty band" for sampled attributions.  

Alex: Sketch of the attribution query I'm thinking — compute per-invocation effective cost then rollup windows for amortized credits:  
```sql
-- per-invocation econ rough prototype
SELECT
  invocation_id,
  route_id,
  model_sku,
  tokens_in + tokens_out AS tokens_total,
  model_unit_price,
  CASE WHEN cache_hit THEN tokens_total * model_unit_price * cache_credit_pct ELSE tokens_total * model_unit_price END AS post_cache_cost,
  CASE WHEN quantized THEN (tokens_total * model_unit_price) * quant_multiplier ELSE tokens_total * model_unit_price END AS quant_adjusted_cost
FROM invocation_events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '7 days';
```
This gives us a base to derive "savings = baseline_cost - observed_cost" and then apply split rules.  

Maria: Two notes: (1) Baseline needs to be clearly defined (non-quantized public model price?) (2) For fallback cases where multiple models are tried in one request, attribute to last-serving model but show a breakdown row for the attempt chain so engs can debug.  

Sam: For implementation, we should tag each request with route_decision_id and cache_decision_id so we can join joinability. That lets us compute "first-hit route" vs "final-serve route" without heuristics.  

Rafi: Canary traffic edgecase — do not amortize canary credits into mainline tenant economics. Show canary as separate column + option to merge/ignore.  

Ciara: UX: add a toggle on the panel: [Direct credits] vs [Amortized credits]. default to amortized for higher-level dashboards, direct for per-route drilldowns. Also add a tiny explainer tooltip: "Amortized credits spread cache-prefetch benefits over N hours to reduce volatility."  

Alex: Sounds actionable. Plan: (1) implement per-invocation query (proto) (2) add route_decision_id tag in proxy (Sam) (3) console panel with toggle & three-bucket breakdown (Ciara + Maria) (4) behind feature flag econ-v2 experiment.  I'll open a PR with the query + mock panels.  

Sam: I'll add route_decision_id and cache_decision_id fields to the proxy traces. ETA: today.  

Rafi: I'll write the model_sku mapping table to ensure quantized variants map to their baseline SKU and unit_price.  

Ciara: I can mock the UI copy and the uncertainty band visuals. want to avoid too much math on the card.  

Maria: one more ask — show a small "audit trail" link per route that expands the raw events for a sample invocation. helps CS and SRE when customers question bills.  

Alex: 👍 will add audit-trail link.  

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: econ-v2/query-proto -> staging in 30m (build 2026.03.20.14).  

Sam: :thumbsup:  

Rafi: thanks all — will sync after proxy change lands.
